summary: Adversarially review the round-9 paper edits (C7 default *3, T46 fixes) against the evidence files

confirmed.problem: As written this says that ten-pawn rings on C7 are *3, which reads as all of them. Only eight ten-pawn rings are known to be *3. The scanned 5+5 outcome histogram shows most rings are other values: 63 are *2 and the rest are N, P, L or R of other kinds. The abstract's "ten-pawn rings reach star three" is fine, but the intro bullet is not.
confirmed.evidence: research/star26_rings/c7/p10_5_5/MERGE.txt: 90,313,025 rows, default_setting_hits 71, default_star2 63, default_star3plus 8. Section 8 itself says "finds eight of value *3".
confirmed.fix: Write "some ten-pawn rings on C7 are *3", or "a ten-pawn ring on C7 is *3".

verdict.reason: The defect is real but small. In 01_intro.tex line 46, "on $\cyl{7}$ ten-pawn rings are $\nim{3}$" is a bare plural, which reads as a statement about all ten-pawn rings on C7. The evidence says otherwise. research/star26_rings/c7/p10_5_5/MERGE.txt has 90,313,025 rows of 5+5 rings. Only 8 are *3 (8 "N,3" lines) and 63 are *2. The rest are L, R, N or P of other values, with 66.2M N, 11.9M L, 11.9M R and 0.22M P in the default outcome histogram. Section 8 (08_star2.tex, around line 151) says correctly "finds eight of value $\nim{3}$", so the intro bullet overstates its own source. I looked for a reading that saves it. The neighbouring clause, "a six-pawn ring suffices", is an explicit existential, and the abstract's "ten-pawn rings reach star three" says "reach", which is existential. But the intro bullet is the only place with a bare "are", and it is the line a reader would quote. The edit is this round's, so it counts. The other claims in the sentence hold up: eight *3 rings on C7 in the default setting, and the C2 label matches the paper's own definition. The abstract wording is acceptable and needs no change.
verdict.better_fix:
In paper/ieee/sections/01_intro.tex lines 46-47, replace "and on $\cyl{7}$ ten-pawn rings are
  $
im{3}$ \lab{C2}." with "and on $\cyl{7}$ a ten-pawn ring can be
  $
im{3}$ \lab{C2}." This parallels "a six-pawn ring suffices" earlier in the same bullet. "Some ten-pawn rings on $\cyl{7}$ are $
im{3}$" would also work. Optionally, change the abstract to "some ten-pawn rings reach star three" for symmetry. It is not wrong as it stands.

confirmed.quote: If a side is drawn, the \emph{draw treatment} counts that draw as a win for black, as a win for white, or as worth $0$.
confirmed.problem: The third draw treatment is not defined by the new definition. A drawn side 'worth 0' does not say what the end position becomes when the other side is a win, a loss or also a draw. The text gives rules only for +BIG, -BIG, {+BIG|-BIG} and 0.
confirmed.evidence: realchess/oracle_value.py pair_game, kind 'draw0', gives {BIG*r_W | BIG*r_B} with a draw as 0. That is {0|-BIG}, {BIG|0} or * for draw/draw. None of these follows from the paper's sentence, and a reader could take 'worth 0' to mean the whole end position is 0. Lemma 18 and Theorem 19(b), (c) are unaffected: (b) holds under 'free' and (c) uses the black-win treatment. Only the definition is incomplete, and (b) says 'every draw treatment'. realchess/REPORT.md section 6 says the draw-as-0 value is not pinned.
confirmed.fix: Say what 'worth 0' does: 'or as worth 0, so that a drawn side contributes 0 and the end position is {BIG r_W | BIG r_B}, where r_W and r_B in {-1,0,1} are the results for White with white and with black to move'.

verdict.reason:
The gap is real but low-severity. I could not refute it. Line 12 of 09_real.tex gives explicit rules only for +BIG, -BIG, {+BIG|-BIG} and 0. It maps a drawn side to a win for black or a win for white. Those two treatments reduce to the four explicit rules, so they are fully defined. For "or as worth 0" it says only that the draw is "worth 0". It never says how a drawn side combines with the other side. The mixed cases are draw/win, draw/loss and draw/draw, for example white to move draws and black to move wins. The rules before it do not cover them, since they need both sides to be wins or losses. So the third treatment is under-specified, and a reader could take "worth 0" to make the whole end position 0.

realchess/oracle_value.py (pair_game, kind "draw0", lines 630-645) confirms the intended meaning. If both sides are wins for White the position is +BIG, and if both are wins for Black it is -BIG. Otherwise it is {BIG*rW | BIG*rB}, where rW and rB are in {-1,0,1} and a draw counts as 0. That gives {0|-BIG}, {BIG|0}, {0|BIG}=1 and {0|0}=*. The same formula also reproduces the paper's N rule, {BIG|-BIG}, and its P rule, {-BIG|BIG}=0. realchess/REPORT.md lines 33 and 118 describe the treatment as "draws counted as 0".

What the gap does not affect:
- The claim "All these games lie between -2BIG and 2BIG" holds for the code's games.
- Lemma 18 (sandwich) does not depend on which treatment is meant.
- Theorem 19(b) rests on the "free" treatment, where every non-L/R terminal is any game in [-2BIG, 2BIG], so it covers whatever "worth 0" means (REPORT.md line 26).
- Theorem 19(c) uses the black-win treatment, which is fully defined.
- The intro's "however draws are treated" is also covered by (b).

So only the definition is incomplete. The reviewer's fix is correct, since a drawn side means at least one of rW, rB is 0 and the {BIG|BIG} problem cannot arise. I tightened the wording below.

The prose below omits the "\lab" tags and the reviewer's "so that".
verdict.better_fix: In 09_real.tex line 12, replace "or as worth $0$." with: "or as worth $0$; in the last case the end position is $\game{\BIG r_W}{\BIG r_B}$, where $r_W,r_B\in\{-1,0,1\}$ are White's results with white and with black to move." The sentence "All these games lie between $-2\BIG$ and $2\BIG$." follows unchanged. Example: draw with white to move and a black win with black to move gives $\game{0}{-\BIG}$, and two drawn sides give $\ast$.

confirmed.quote:
at once: a8=Q is mate: it checks along the a-file, and its wrapped diagonals and the white king cover every flight
square \lab{C2}.
confirmed.problem: The new sentence chains two colons ('wins at once: a8=Q is mate: it checks'), which is a punctuation slip introduced by the edit. It is also imprecise. The wrapped diagonals and the white king do not cover a4: that flight square is covered only because it lies on the checking a-file.
confirmed.evidence: odd_cylinders_verify/REPORT.md section 3.2 and the re-derivation in the T46 verdict: the queen's two wrapped diagonals are a8-b7-c6-a5-b4-c3-a2-b1 and a8-c7-b6-a5-c4-b3-a2-c1. They cover b3, b4, c3, c4 and a2. The white king covers a2, b2 and c2. a4 lies on the a-file between the queen and the black king, so a king step there stays in check. The mate itself and the C3 result are correct.
confirmed.fix: Write: 'wins at once, since a8=Q is mate: it checks along the a-file, which also covers a4, and its wrapped diagonals and the white king cover the other flight squares'.

verdict.reason:
The defect is real, but low severity. I checked it against the evidence and by enumerating the flight squares of Ka3 on a 3-file cylinder after Ka1, Qa8.

- **Wrong attribution:** the paper (10_tablebases.tex, line 143) says "its wrapped diagonals and the white king cover every flight square". That is false for a4. The white king (a1) covers only a2, b2 and c2. The wrapped diagonals cover only b3, b4, c3 and c4. a4 is covered by neither. It is covered only because it lies on the a-file between the queen and the black king, so a king step there stays in check. research/odd_cylinders_verify/REPORT.md (lines 256-261) confirms this ("the queen covers a4 on its file and b3, c3, b4, c4 on its two wrapped diagonals").
- **Mate and C3 result stand:** the move a8=Q is mate and the C3 result is correct. Only the explanation is imprecise.
- **Chained colon:** "wins at once: a8=Q is mate: it checks ..." is the only double-colon sentence in the sections, so it is a real punctuation slip from this edit. The old text, "a8=Q mates along a wrapped diagonal", was also wrong, because the check is along the a-file. The edit moved toward the truth but left the a4 misattribution.

I could not refute the claim. A generous reader could take "cover" to include the a-file check, but the sentence names the diagonals and the king as the coverers.
verdict.better_fix: Replace the sentence in 10_tablebases.tex lines 142-144 with: "On $\cyl{3}$, Ka1, Pa7 against Ka3 wins at once, since a8=Q is mate: it checks along the a-file, which also covers a4, its wrapped diagonals cover b3, b4, c3 and c4, and the white king covers a2, b2 and c2 \lab{C2}." This removes the double colon, assigns each flight square to the right piece, and matches REPORT.md. The reviewer's shorter version ("...which also covers a4, and its wrapped diagonals and the white king cover the other flight squares") is also correct and a smaller edit.

confirmed.problem: The bare plural reads as a universal claim. Only some ten-pawn rings on C7 are *3. The next clause in the same bullet ('a six-pawn ring suffices') is existential, and the abstract's 'reach star three' is correct. The intro bullet is not.
confirmed.evidence: research/star26_rings/c7/p10_5_5/MERGE.txt: 71 default-setting hits among about 90 million 5+5 ten-pawn roots, of which 63 are *2 and 8 are *3. 08_star2.tex line 151 says 'finds eight of value *3'.
confirmed.fix: Write 'and on $\cyl{7}$ some ten-pawn rings are $\nim{3}$' or 'ten-pawn rings reach $\nim{3}$'.

verdict.reason: Could not refute it. The intro bullet (01_intro.tex line 46) says "on $\cyl{7}$ ten-pawn rings are $\nim{3}$". A bare plural reads as a universal claim, and the evidence is existential. research/star26_rings/c7/p10_5_5/MERGE.txt covers 90,313,025 roots with five pawns a side. So the intro bullet contradicts the body. It also sits beside the existential "a six-pawn ring suffices" in the same bullet. The scope is low: the \lab{C2} label matches the section's check of those eight, and the wording is the only problem.

that none exists with six pawns or fewer in the default setting, and that $\nim{2}$

confirmed.evidence: 08_star2.tex lines 133-134: 'On C3 the only ring *2 with six pawns in the default setting is W a2 a3 b2 / B b7 c6 c7'. The abstract and intro scope the census claim to ordinary boards of width at most four.
confirmed.fix: Write 'that none exists on an ordinary board of width at most four with six pawns or fewer in the default setting'.

verdict.reason: I could not refute it. The opener at 08_star2.tex lines 3-6 asks about "a board with eight ranks" and says "none exists with six pawns or fewer in the default setting" with no board-width scope. The same section (lines 133-134) gives a six-pawn *2 ring on the three-file cylinder, W a2 a3 b2 / B b7 c6 c7, in the default setting, confirmed at C2. Line 139 itself says it has one pawn fewer than any ordinary board of width at most four allows. The third clause, "*2 appears with seven", is false for the same reason. Read in context, the clause is true only for the census, which atlas Section 06 defines as ordinary boards of width 1-4. The abstract, the intro bullet at 01_intro.tex line 45, line 111, and the conclusion all carry that scope, so the opener is now the odd one out. The only possible rebuttal is to read "none exists" as picking up "in the census" from the first clause. That reading is unnatural, because the sentence sits under the 8-rank board question and the cylinder is such a board. Caveat for triage: the opener is pre-existing text. The round9b patch has no hunk in lines 1-10 of 08_star2.tex. The abstract and intro already carried the width scope before this round, so this round does not newly contradict it. Severity is low, and it matters only if the orchestrator's filter allows pre-existing text that is inconsistent with the scoped abstract and intro.
verdict.better_fix: In 08_star2.tex lines 4-6, put the scope ahead of both clauses so it governs "none exists" and "appears with seven". Replace "that none exists with six pawns or fewer in the default setting, and that $\nim{2}$ appears with seven." with "that on ordinary boards of width at most four none exists with six pawns or fewer in the default setting, and that $\nim{2}$ appears with seven." This is slightly better than scoping only the first clause as the reviewer proposes, because it also fixes "appears with seven", which the three-file cylinder ring contradicts. The wording matches line 111, the intro, and the abstract. The subsection titles at lines 46 and 58 can stay, because the census theorem and Theorem star2seven are scoped.

The body (08_star2.tex lines 151-154) finds only eight in a partial scan of the five-a-side rings. The C2 label also covers only the whole-board values. verdict.reason: Real, but narrower than reported. Intro line 46-47 says "on $\cyl{7}$ ten-pawn rings are $\nim{3}$", a bare plural that reads as every ten-pawn ring. Only eight rings out of the 90,313,025 scanned roots are *3 (MERGE.txt), and 63 of the other default-setting hits are *2. The body (08_star2.tex lines 151-154) and the abstract ("ten-pawn rings reach star three") state it existentially, so the intro bullet is the one overgeneral line. Its sibling clause "a six-pawn ring suffices" is also existential. The evidence supports the C2 label for the whole-board values of all eight: delegate/checks/c7p10/s3_*_nosplit.txt (cylcgt) shows *3 for all eight, delegate/checks/c7_star3/t43_*.txt (the independent Codex solver) shows P(G+*3)=1 for all eight, and the scanner lists them. It lists its headline values explicitly, and *3 on $\cyl{7}$ exists in both models (six of the eight survive as sums), so no *3 clause needs adding there. verdict.better_fix: In /Users/aritro/Downloads/Research/Chessendgames/paper/ieee/sections/01_intro.tex line 46-47, write "and on $\cyl{7}$ some ten-pawn rings are $\nim{3}$ \lab{C2}". "ten-pawn rings reach $\nim{3}$" would also do, to match the abstract. No change is needed to the C2 label or to 05_sums.tex.

confirmed.quote: counts that draw as a win for black, as a win for white, or as worth 0
confirmed.problem: The rewritten Definition lets the draw treatment act on one drawn side, but the third treatment is not parallel to the other two. A single side cannot be 'worth 0'. The text does not say what end position results when one side is decisive and the other is drawn (for example white to move wins, black to move draws). Theorem (b), 'under every draw treatment', and the sandwich lemma depend on this definition.
confirmed.evidence: The old definition used one fixed game t for every undecided end position, which was unambiguous. The new one maps four fully decided cases (+BIG, -BIG, {+BIG|-BIG}, 0). For a mixed end position, 'win for black' and 'win for white' are clear, but '0' could mean the whole end position is 0 or that the mover loses on that side. The two readings give different trees.
confirmed.fix: State the third treatment explicitly, for example 'or as a loss for the side to move, so a position drawn on both sides is worth 0'. Alternatively, say that the whole end position is replaced by 0.

verdict.reason:
Partly real, low-to-medium severity, and the reviewer's suggested fixes are wrong. I read /Users/aritro/Downloads/Research/Chessendgames/paper/ieee/sections/09_real.tex lines 7-14 against the implementation in /Users/aritro/Downloads/Research/Chessendgames/realchess/oracle_value.py (pair_game, TREATMENTS, lines 621-644).

What survives: the first two treatments are unambiguous. Each drawn side becomes a win for black or for white, and the four-case list then fixes the end position. That matches the code's "switch" kind, which substitutes the draw per side. The third treatment is not fixed by the text. The four-case list only covers sides that are both decisive, so for white to move wins and black to move draws, "worth 0" gives no end position. Claims that quantify over every draw treatment, such as Theorem (b) and the Sandwich lemma, therefore rest on an under-specified object. The sandwich bounds themselves still hold. Every leaf is between -2BIG and 2BIG under any reading, so the numerical claims are not endangered.

What is wrong in the reviewer's account: a single side can be worth 0, and the code does exactly that. For the "draw = 0" treatment, pair_game builds {BIG*rw | BIG*rb}, where a drawn side has r = 0. The drawn side's option is the game 0. Its docstring gives the examples draw/Black-win = {0 | -BIG} and draw/draw = *. Neither of the reviewer's readings matches this:
- Replacing the whole end position by 0 would make {0 | -BIG} equal 0, and it would make draw/draw equal 0 instead of *.
- Treating the drawn side as a loss for the side to move would make white-draw/black-win equal {|-BIG} = -BIG instead of {0 | -BIG}. Draw/draw would again be 0 instead of *.

The reviewer's suggested wording would therefore make the paper disagree with the computed "draw = 0" runs. The fix must state the per-side rule.

Fix, replacing the sentence at lines 12-13:
"If a side is drawn, the \emph{draw treatment} counts that draw as a win for black, as a win for white, or as a result worth $0$; in the last case the drawn side leaves its mover the option $0$, so white to move winning and black to move drawing gives $\game{+\BIG}{0}$, and two drawn sides give $\star$."
The macro \game takes two arguments, so \game{+\BIG}{0} compiles. Keep "All these games lie between $-2\BIG$ and $2\BIG$." as it is.
verdict.better_fix: In 09_real.tex lines 12-13, replace "counts that draw as a win for black, as a win for white, or as worth $0$." with "counts that draw as a win for black, as a win for white, or as a result worth $0$; in the last case the drawn side leaves its mover the option $0$, so white to move winning and black to move drawing gives $\game{+\BIG}{0}$, and two drawn sides give $\star$." Do not adopt the reviewer's "loss for the side to move" wording or the "whole end position is 0" wording. Both contradict realchess/oracle_value.py, where draw/draw is star and white-draw/black-win is {0 | -BIG}.

confirmed.quote: a8=Q is mate: it checks along the a-file
confirmed.problem: Voice break: two colons chain in one sentence ('wins at once: a8=Q is mate: it checks ...'), and the claim runs on with three clauses. In the same paragraph 'and with 9 and 10 \lab{C1}' drops the noun 'files' after 'with 4 to 8 files'.
confirmed.evidence: 10_tablebases.tex lines 141-144. The mate itself is correct. On C3, a8=Q checks along the a-file, and its wrapped diagonals plus the white king cover b3, b4, c3, c4, a2, b2 and c2. The plain-voice rule in REVISION_PLAN section 5 asks for short clauses.
confirmed.fix: Write 'wins at once, since a8=Q is mate: it checks along the a-file, and its wrapped diagonals and the white king cover every flight square \lab{C2}'. Write 'and with 9 and 10 files \lab{C1}'.

verdict.reason: Partly real, low severity. The double colon is genuine: line 143 is the only sentence in the paper with two colons ('wins at once: a8=Q is mate: it checks ...'). It also runs three clauses together, against the short-clause rule in REVISION_PLAN section 5. The second half of the report is not a defect. 'with 4 to 8 files, and with 9 and 10' is ordinary coordinate ellipsis and reads fine. The labels are right (C2 for n<=8, C1 for 9 and 10), and the mate is correct. I checked it on C3 with a small script (queen a8, king a1, black king a3). The a-file check is the only check. The old wording 'mates along a wrapped diagonal' was wrong, and the new wording fixes it. The reviewer's proposed fix would still leave a literal inaccuracy in the same sentence. The black king's eight flight squares are a2, a4, b2, b3, b4, c2, c3 and c4. The wrapped diagonals and the white king cover seven of them (a2, b2, b3, b4, c2, c3, c4). Square a4 is covered only by the queen along the a-file. So 'its wrapped diagonals and the white king cover every flight square' is false as written for a4. The reviewer's own list of covered squares leaves out a4. Rewrite the sentence so it names who covers what.
verdict.better_fix: In /Users/aritro/Downloads/Research/Chessendgames/paper/ieee/sections/10_tablebases.tex, replace lines 142-144 ('and with 9 and 10 \lab{C1}. On $\cyl{3}$, Ka1, Pa7 against Ka3 wins at once: a8=Q is mate: it checks ... square \lab{C2}.') with: 'and with 9 and 10 \lab{C1}. On $\cyl{3}$, Ka1, Pa7 against Ka3 wins at once, since a8=Q is mate. The queen checks along the a-file, which also covers a4; its wrapped diagonals cover b3, b4, c3 and c4, and the white king covers a2, b2 and c2 \lab{C2}.' This leaves no double colon and states all eight flight squares correctly. The 'with 9 and 10' clause can stay as it is, or become 'with 9 and 10 files' if the author prefers.

confirmed.quote: as a sum and as a whole board
confirmed.problem: Inconsistent term for one concept. The same paragraph says 'our engine as a whole-board game' (line 153), and line 117 says 'As whole-board games'. The naming table in REVISION_PLAN section 5 fixes 'sum model; whole-board game'. This sentence also stacks three commas and two 'and's, so it is hard to parse.
confirmed.evidence: 08_star2.tex lines 144-146: 'our engine, as a sum and as a whole board, and the independent whole-board solver agree'. Line 153: 'our engine as a whole-board game'.
confirmed.fix: Write 'our engine, as a sum and as a whole-board game, and the independent whole-board solver agree'. Alternatively, reword to 'our engine (as a sum and with splitting switched off) and the independent whole-board solver agree'.

verdict.reason: The defect is real but low severity. The facts are not in doubt. delegate/checks/a_plus_star/results.txt shows the position solved three ways: cylcgt as a sum (*3), cylcgt with splitting off (*3), and the Codex solver (*3). Codex wrote the independent whole-board solver, so the sentence is supported. The problem is wording only. The naming table in REVISION_PLAN section 5 fixes "sum model; whole-board game". The paper follows that in line 117 ("As whole-board games") and line 153 ("our engine as a whole-board game"), and 05_sums.tex defines W(X) as "the whole-board game". Line 145 alone says "as a whole board". That is not a usable noun phrase: a position is not "a whole board", and elsewhere the paper writes "on the whole board". The sentence also stacks three commas and two "and"s, so the subject and the two modes of the engine are hard to separate. The "on the whole board" wording in Section V is not a counterexample, because it is a different construction. The reviewer's first suggested fix cures the term but keeps the comma stack.
verdict.better_fix: In 08_star2.tex, lines 144-146, replace "and our engine, as a sum and as a whole board, and the independent whole-board solver agree" with "and our engine as a sum, our engine as a whole-board game and the independent whole-board solver agree". This reuses the term from line 153 and removes the nested commas.

confirmed.quote: There the model is the only judge; certified components beyond
confirmed.problem: Open problem 7 no longer states a problem. The engine finding moved into the summary paragraph, so 'There' has no antecedent beyond the item's title. The item does not say which question is open, even though the section announces 'Seven problems are open'.
confirmed.evidence: 14_conclusion.tex lines 34-35. The item now reads only '\emph{Engines beyond the tablebases.} There the model is the only judge; certified components beyond seven men would give real-chess ground truth.'
confirmed.fix: State the question, for example 'On sums of 15 to 20 men no tablebase judges the engines; do their misses survive certified real-chess components beyond seven men?'.

verdict.reason: The defect is real but low severity. This round's edit moved the engine finding (engines often miss the model's winning moves on sums of 15 to 20 men) out of item 7 and into the summary paragraph at lines 7-9. Item 7 (lines 34-35) now reads only "There the model is the only judge; certified components beyond seven men would give real-chess ground truth." Its sole antecedent for "There" is the italic title "Engines beyond the tablebases". The item never names the engines, the sums, or the question. The summary paragraph supplies that context about 25 lines earlier, but the list is meant to stand on its own after "Seven problems are open", and the old version was self-contained. I tried to refute it on three grounds. First, other items are task-like rather than questions (item 5, "KPKP and KPPK on the cylinder come next"), so the lack of a question mark is not itself a flaw. Second, "there" already appeared in the old wording ("but there the model is the only judge"). Third, 12_engines.tex ends its "Engines on Sums" subsection with "Proving real-chess errors would need the kind of certification that Section~\ref{sec:real} begins for $1/8$", so the substance is supported. These points show the claim is true and supported, but they do not restore the missing statement of what is open. The reviewer's "no longer states a problem" is somewhat overstated, since the remedy is still implicit. I found no false statement, broken reference or wrong label in the item.
verdict.better_fix: Replace lines 34-35 of 14_conclusion.tex with: "\item \emph{Engines beyond the tablebases.} Are the engines' misses on sums of 15 to 20 men errors in real chess? No tablebase judges those positions and the model is the only judge there; certified components beyond seven men would give real-chess ground truth." This is the reviewer's idea in the paper's voice. It names the question and keeps the original remedy clause.

rejected.quote: So $\nim{3}$, like $\nim{2}$, needs no more than eight ranks.
rejected.why:
The reviewer's claim does not hold, for three reasons.

1. The sentence is about ranks, and the paper counts the cylinder as an eight-rank board.
- 02_rules.tex defines both $\cyl{n}$ and $\flatb{n}$ as the board "with $n$ files and eight ranks".
- The intro states the $\nim{2}$ question as one about "an 8-rank board".
- The conclusion's open problem asks for "a $\nim{4}$ on eight ranks", so the paper itself measures the question in ranks and not in whether the board is flat.
- A single-component $\nim{3}$ on $\cyl{7}$ is therefore a $\nim{3}$ with eight ranks, so "needs no more than eight ranks" follows.
- The cut lemma (a ring cannot be flattened) only matters for the ordinary-board claim. The sentence does not make that claim, and the paper's ordinary-board statement stays in the next paragraph and is limited to $\nim{2}$.

2. The $\nim{3}$ on eight ranks was not introduced this round.
- The unchanged lines 143-145 already give A plus a $\star$ group, a $\nim{3}$ on six files of the ordinary board with nine pawns.
- So any tension with line 157 ("Elkies' higher nimbers need larger boards") already existed before this round's edits.
- The new sentence adds the single-component $\nim{3}$ at eight ranks, and nothing in this round's text makes that contradiction worse.

3. Line 157 is not contradicted.
- It was not touched by the patch. The conclusion's open $\nim{4}$-on-eight-ranks problem fixes its scope: "Elkies' higher nimbers" reads as the nimbers Elkies built on large boards, which is what intro line 22 says.
- Finding a $\nim{3}$ at eight ranks does not deny that his constructions need larger boards.

The sentence is somewhat redundant with the A plus $\star$ result, but redundancy is taste, not a defect. Its premise is also supported: the eight $\cyl{7}$ ten-pawn positions are labelled \lab{C2}, backed by three solvers, and the intro and abstract match.

If the author wants a tweak, "Elkies' constructions of higher nimbers use larger boards" in line 157 would remove any ambiguity. That is optional.

I read the patch and the full text of 08_star2.tex, the intro, the rules section, the conclusion and the abstract. I did not re-run the C7 evidence.

rejected.quote: The two models agree on every headline value:
rejected.why: The facts are right but the sentence is not false or contradicted. In delegate/checks/c7p10, s3_3_sum and s3_8_sum give {0,*2|0,*} and {0,*|0,*2}, the other six sums give *3, and all eight nosplit runs give *3. Section 8 (08_star2.tex lines 151-154) already states both facts: the example ring is "*3 in both models" and "as sums of components six keep the value". Line 137 of 05_sums.tex is a colon-introduced list. It claims agreement for the 1/8 and up-second-star positions in all nine settings and for the seven-pawn *2 in the default setting, and every item is true. It was not edited this round and makes no claim about the C7 rings. It was never a universal over the abstract's headlines either: Tiny 1 and the six-pawn C3 ring *2, both abstract/intro headlines, were never in it. The abstract and intro claim only that ten-pawn C7 rings reach *3. That is an existence claim, witnessed in both models by six of the eight rings, including the displayed one. The next sentence ("Elsewhere they can differ, even in outcome") and the closing "Where they differ, we name the model we mean" cover the two sum-model exceptions, and Section 8 names them where the claim is made. Section 8 treats the five-file *2 scan the same way (15 of 21 keep the value as sums), with no contradiction in Section 5. A reader cannot take Section 5 to promise sum-model agreement for the *3 rings.

rejected.quote: a partial scan of the ten-pawn rings with five pawns a side finds eight of value
rejected.why: The evidence is accurate but the sentence is not false or unsupported, so this is taste rather than a defect. Confirmed: the 5+5 split is complete (1024 of 1024 subchunks merged, 90,313,025 roots, 8 hits all at N,3, none higher). The 4+6 scan is still running (173 of 1024 summaries). The eight positions are four colour-reversed pairs: a file-symmetry plus colour-reversal check pairs 1-5, 2-6, 3-7 and 4-8 of c7_star3/positions.txt. But "partial scan of the ten-pawn rings" is true as written. The scan covers only part of the ten-pawn rings, namely the 5+5 split, and the phrase "with five pawns a side" names that part. The paper claims only that eight *3 rings exist in the default setting on C7, and "partial" correctly marks eight as a lower bound for all ten-pawn rings. The remaining claims in the sentence hold: all eight give G+*3 as a P-position in the T43 solver. The whole-board cylcgt runs give *3 for all eight. Six of the eight keep *3 as sums (positions 3 and 8, a colour-reversed pair, change to {0,*2|0,*} and {0,*|0,*2}). The stated *3 "in both models" for position 1 is correct (nosplit and sum both *3). The only way to misread it is to take the 5+5 split as itself incomplete. That misreading is conservative, since it makes a reader treat eight as a minimum, and it changes no claim in the abstract, intro or Section VIII. Not saying "four pairs" is also not a defect: the paper counts twins as separate positions, as in "two *2 positions, A and its color-reversed twin B" and "six ... three and the other three are twins". The C6 sentence's twin remark is a style choice, not a required parallel. The reviewer's fix adds "the other splits are unfinished", a work-in-progress note in a paper meant to read as final (no placeholders). It would go stale when the 4+6, 3+7, 2+8 and 1+9 splits finish.

rejected.quote: \lab{C2}; as sums of components six keep the value.
rejected.why:
The evidence matches the reviewer, but the text does not do what the reviewer says. Evidence first. delegate/checks/c7p10/s3_*_sum.txt are cylcgt-only outputs, and the T43 solver outputs (delegate/checks/c7_star3/t43_*.txt) test G+*k as a whole board. Six of the eight sums give *3 (s3_1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7). s3_3 gives {0,*2|0,*} and s3_8 gives {0,*|0,*2}. So "six keep the value" is true, and it rests on one program.

The label does not cover that clause. In 08_star2.tex the paper puts \lab{...} at the end of the claim it certifies ("... agree \lab{C2}."). Here \lab{C2} closes the clause "the scanner, our engine as a whole-board game and a third solver written from the rules agree", and the semicolon starts a new, unlabeled clause. The text asserts C2 only for the whole-board agreement, which the scanner, cylcgt with splitting off and t43_*.txt (P(G+*3)=1 for all eight) do support.

The same convention already holds for sum-model counts that this round did not touch. Line 118 reads "As sums of components ... $15$ keep the value; the other six change only through the splitting", with no label. Line 124 reads "these are $\nim{2}$ in both models", also unlabeled. A \lab{C1} on the new clause would be inconsistent with those lines unless they were changed too. The count is also a side detail rather than a headline number, and the intro asks for labels on headline numbers.

At most this is a scoping nitpick. It is not a false or mislabeled statement.

rejected.quote: a third solver written from the rules
rejected.why:
Not a real defect, and the proposed fix would make the text false.

1. The third checker is a different program from every name the paper already uses. delegate/checks/c7_star3/run.sh and research/c7_independent/REPORT.md show it is T43's c7check.c. Codex wrote it from the rules alone, and the orchestrator extended it to test heaps 0-5 (c7k_persist). It is a C7-specific tester of whether G+*k is a second-player win.
   - "The independent whole-board solver" is verify_ext/codex/solver.py (a Python canonical-form solver). The A+star check at 08_star2.tex:145 used it, and delegate/checks/a_plus_star/results.txt shows "codex *3 31s". The same name is used at 08_star2.tex:54 and :106.
   - "An independent C solver" (07_targets.tex:30, 08_star2.tex:53) is the atlas/flat8/rerun program (RESULTS.md:59).
   - "An independent ring solver" is research/ring_min_independent/ring.c.
   - The C7 checker is none of these. Calling it "the independent whole-board solver" would credit a Python solver with a check it never ran, so the suggested fix introduces a false statement.

2. The wording is not ambiguous in the way the reviewer says. The sentence lists the scanner, our engine as a whole-board game, and "a third solver", so "third" marks a program distinct from the first two. The phrase has the same form as "a third, separately written solver" at 07_targets.tex:70 and the descriptive "an independent ring solver" at :136. The paper already describes its per-task checkers descriptively, not by a fixed name.

3. The C2 label does not depend on the identity. C2 only needs two independently written programs to agree, and this sentence has three, whichever program the third is.

4. The Acknowledgment gap the reviewer points to is real but separate from this defect. It credits Codex only with "the independent whole-board solver and the census scanner that found the seven-pawn positions". It does not cover c7check or the ten-pawn C7 scanner runs, and the same is true of the other per-task checkers.

The evidence otherwise supports the sentence. All eight positions in delegate/checks/c7_star3/positions.txt give P(G+*3)=1 and no other heap from 0 to 5 in t43_1..8.txt. The REVIEW.md C7 entry says six of eight keep *3 as a sum.

rejected.quote: Outside the default setting it comes early
rejected.why:
I could not make the claim hold. "Early" is not unsupported, and the stand-alone sentence is not orphaned.

1. "Early" has a clear referent in the paragraph and section. The paper's frame is the cylinder width n: "Narrower cylinders need fewer pawns", and the first ring *2 on C_n has n+3 pawns. Both non-default *3 examples sit on narrower cylinders than the default one: the eight-pawn ring on C4 and the ten-pawn ring on C3, against C7 in the default setting. The next sentence, "In the default setting it appears on C7", names the contrast directly. The reviewer concedes that "the only difference is the narrower cylinder". That difference is what "early" says, so the examples support it.

2. The reviewer's pawn-count point does not make the sentence false. The C3 ring has ten pawns, the same as the C7 ring. The text never says "fewer pawns", and the C4 example does use fewer (eight).

3. The sentence "Rings give *3 in a single component" is not orphaned. It is a true topic sentence. The C4 and C3 rings, the C7 rings and the default-setting position A beside a * group in the previous sentence all fit it. The removed qualifier "but so far only outside the default setting" became false once the C7 default rings were found, so removing it was correct.

4. The terse style matches the surrounding text ("A *3 lies just beyond these scans", "Narrower cylinders need fewer pawns").

The examples I could check against RESULTS.md match the text: C4 with eight pawns (opponent rule, e.p. off) and C3 with ten pawns (count rule, e.p. off). RESULTS.md predates the C7 result, so I could not check the C7 claim there. The remaining objection is a wording preference, not a false or unsupported statement, a wrong label, a broken reference or a voice break.

rejected.quote: pieces taking the other missing men; we checked these histories by hand
rejected.why:
The defect does not hold up. It is a wording and labeling preference, not a false or unsupported statement.

1. **The convention is named.** "pieces taking the other missing men" states that the missing men other than the one taken by the file-shift capture are taken by pieces. That is the covering convention. The phrase is a grammatical absolute construction, not a dangling modifier, and the suggested "being taken by pieces" is a taste edit.

2. **The label rule does not apply here.** Section I says "Theorems and headline numbers carry labels." A legality statement is neither. Section VII-B states its histories ("c2×b3, b3--b4--b5--b6, a7--a6 and c7--c5") with no label, and the Fig. 6 caption says "legal pawn history" with no label. The claim that the paper labels every other verification statement is therefore false. This round's change is the correct one. Before it, the legality claim sat inside the C2-labeled theorem. REVIEW_LOG R11 records that no repo file records more than the geometry, so a C2 label there was unearned. Moving it to plain prose and saying "by hand" is the honest treatment, and no label in the P, AI, C2, C1, Conj scheme fits a hand check.

3. **The statement matches the evidence.** I ran `pawnhist.min_captures` on A plus T and B plus T. A needs exactly one white file-shift capture and no black one. B needs exactly one black file-shift capture and no white one. This is the single capture the text names, c2×d3 for A and b7×a6 for B. The color-reversed, file-mirrored correspondence checks out too: the mirror of c2×d3 is b7×a6.

4. **There is no contradiction with T32.** research/five_file_legal/REPORT.md point 7 says the exact pawn-only model would need 5 captures for A, and calls that "a remark about the paper's convention, not a verified error." The paper's text uses the covering model and says so, so the two do not conflict. T32 covers other positions, not A and B.

5. **"By hand" does not contradict the intro.** The intro's "we check every position by computer" is about the values of the positions. The hand check is about game history, and the text claims nothing stronger than that.

Nothing in the text is false, and the label placement is correct.

rejected.quote: A search we ran once suggests that real tr\'ebuchets need $h\approx5$--$7$
rejected.why:
The finding is mostly taste, and its one substantive claim, that the verbs contradict, does not hold.

1. Voice. The paper writes in the first person about its own computations: "We searched the census", "We solved ... every component", "We ran Stockfish" (07_targets, 04_kings, 12_engines), and "Our proof of this has a gap." (04_kings). "A search we ran suggests" is the same register. The REVISION_PLAN section 5 ban covers narrative chronology about the document or project ("our first report", "then left", "after these results"). It does not cover stating how a result was obtained. "Once" is the only informal word. It is accurate rather than a voice break: kings/theory/LOOPY.md records the 5 to 7 horizon as "scratch evidence ... one throwaway implementation, hence a CONJECTURE". The edit adds exactly that hedge, and \lab{Conj} is the label the intro defines for it. That is why the edit is an improvement over the old unhedged, unlabelled "Real trébuchets need h≈5–7".

2. Need versus have. This is not a contradiction.
- Both sentences state one claim: the horizon at which the certificate holds for real trébuchets is about 5 to 7. LOOPY.md §5.1 says "(L1) holds for all five White sorties with T ≤ 7 (5 to 7, depending on the sortie)". The same file says "T = 5" for the T-group sortie.
- Both are now hedged ("suggests" in Section IV, "seem to" in the conclusion) and both carry \lab{Conj}.
- The need/have wording predates this round: the old text read "need" in Section IV and "have" in the conclusion. REVISION_PLAN lines 335 and 395 deliberately keep the "T≈5–7" sentence and the "have" phrasing.
- The conclusion cannot read as a contradiction. It sits in a list item that points to Conjecture~\ref{conj:cert} and the horizon conjecture, which define the certificate and h.

3. Consistency with the rest of the paper. "We trust their zero only beside slow or locked components" matches LOOPY.md ("covers only locked or slow contexts") and the Section IV sweep, where 41 of 449 king moves beside the ordinary-board trébuchet draw and 7 win. Nothing the round edited contradicts it.

What remains is that "once" is slightly chatty and the search is not described in the paper. Neither is a false statement, a wrong label, a broken reference or a break from the paper's voice.

The two phrasings are not a defect. They say the same thing in different grammatical slots. "a legal pawn history" is a noun-phrase label, used in the intro bullet (01_intro.tex line 42) and in the Fig. 6 caption (07_targets.tex line 48), which already used it before this round. "can arise in a game" is the verb form in running prose. It appears in 07_targets.tex line 66, also not edited this round, and in the new sentence at 08_star2.tex line 68. That new sentence matches the prose in 07_targets.tex, and its "we checked these histories by hand" ties back to "history" in the caption. The intro change in this round (from "positions that can arise in a game" to "with a legal pawn history") makes the intro agree with the caption. It is also more careful, because in these 10-man positions only the pawn structure is shown to be reachable by 07_targets.tex line 66 and line 82. The kings are frozen in T and the other men are not argued to be reachable. The 08 sentence says "their pawns can arise", which is accurate. Nothing in the text is false, unsupported, mislabelled, a broken reference, or a break in voice, so this is a style preference. Unifying the wording would be taste, and the report should not list it.
